title: Good For You
content: Meaning/Usage: Expressing that you are happy for a person Explanation: This is pretty literal. However, this can be used sarcastically. "Good for you, you finally passed your test." "I heard you got accepted to college, good for you." "I heard you got married recently, good for you." A. "I was really surprised when I was offered the promotion." B. "Why is that?" A. "I just figured it would go to someone with more experience." B. "Good for you, you deserve it as much as anyone." Other Common Sentences "I am proud of you." "All credit goes to you."

examples.sentence: Good for you, you finally passed your test.
I heard you got accepted to college, good for you.
I heard you got married recently, good for you.
I was really surprised when I was offered the promotion.
I just figured it would go to someone with more experience.
Good for you, you deserve it as much as anyone.
